craft_claim: Memory revises upward: recollections become rosier than the lived experience within days. Rosy retrospection is the tone's default distortion - licensable when the text marks whose eye idealizes, but invisible idealization is the mechanism drifting into propaganda.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 33(4):421-448, three investigations (European trip, Thanksgiving vacation, California bicycle trip)
supporting_evidence.note: Across three event studies, expectations were more positive than in-event experience and subsequent recollection was more positive than the experience itself; negative in-event thoughts (distractions, disappointment) fade within days as evaluations brighten.

supporting_evidence.location: Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 51:189-273, self-positivity section
supporting_evidence.note: The review reports that nostalgia increases self-esteem partly by prompting a return to an idealized past, lending lustre to past selves that may not have seemed lustrous at the time - idealization is built into the emotion's self-service.

supporting_evidence.location: Perceptual and Motor Skills 80(1):131-143, survey design
supporting_evidence.note: Batcho's instrument assesses nostalgia for 20 aspects of experience alongside relative judgments of the world past, present, and future - operationalizing nostalgia partly as a comparative evaluation of eras, the same structure behind golden-age thinking (section G).

scope: Idealization mechanics and reliability of remembered scenes; feeds card sections 4-5 and failure analysis.
exceptions: Rosy distortion is a licensed device when focalized (a character's eye, an acknowledged unreliable memory); it fails when the narration presents the idealized past as unqualified fact.
The mirror case - a memory harsher than the truth - signals trauma or grief registers that belong to other tones.
